prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / identity-preserve.
Asset: ONE complete full-body 2D battle character illustration, transparent background.
Input image: approved Wu identity and costume reference. Preserve recognizable face, hair, clothing and accessories; change pose to battle guard. This is a new illustration.
Subject: Wu, young adult fantasy swordswoman. Small youthful fair-skinned face, bright cyan-blue slightly upturned eyes, playful confident grin and one small upper fang. Silver-white smooth hair tightly gathered into a very high ponytail down to mid-calf, grouped sweeping locks, blue satin ribbon bow with two streamers at ponytail root, adjacent black rose, two thin sidelocks down to collarbone, light parted bangs leaving both eyes visible. Matte black round sunglasses rest on her head. Black off-shoulder dress, horizontal neckline ruffle, narrow black waist belt, plain charcoal-black outer skirt with jagged ruffled hem reaching approximately calf length, deep-blue inner lining with light-blue four-pointed stars peeking below the hem. Bare lower legs, black platform ankle boots with folded cuffs and side zippers.
Battle pose and composition: one character facing screen-right at a clear three-quarter side angle, face and gaze toward an opponent outside the right edge. Balanced ready stance, knees slightly flexed, front foot to the right. Her right hand holds ONE drawn slender black longsword in a controlled low forward guard, sword point clearly toward screen-right. Left hand naturally ready near waist. Empty black scabbard strapped diagonally across back. Complete head, ponytail, dress, both boot soles and entire sword visible, comfortable transparent margins. Fit the entire silhouette in a portrait canvas.
Current style direction: masterpiece, best quality, painterly illustration, no lineart, dry impasto brushwork, visible rough brush strokes, broken open edges, muted low-saturation palette with small saturated accents.
Paint in large unified planes, each passage done in a few decisive strokes rather than many small strokes. Build strong value contrast with deep shadow masses and minimal mid-tones, letting small crisp highlights land only on material edges. Hair is drawn in grouped sweeping strokes, with brush marks skipping and breaking over the outer silhouette. The face stays finely rendered with sharp eye highlights, while the body, dress and limbs are kept loosely simplified with broad sketchy planes.
Style priority: confident broad brush masses and strong value design, simplified clothing, selective face detail. Preserve approved character design while applying this current heavier brushwork direction. Muted cool gray cloth and hair, small vivid blue accents in eyes, ribbon and lining; distinguish matte cloth, satin, leather and dark metal.
Background: genuinely transparent RGBA, no scenery, floor, cast shadow, opaque backdrop or painted checkerboard.
Avoid: flat cel shading, smooth airbrush, clean closed contour lines, over-polished rendering, plastic or waxy skin, tiny fragmented brush noise, blurry/extra/missing/fused fingers, deformed face, extra limbs, duplicate characters, extra swords, staff, slash effects, glowing aura, stockings, tights, hair obscuring eyes, sunglasses covering eyes, stars on the outer black skirt, dragging train, cropped feet/hair/weapon, text, signature, watermark, border, collage or multiple views.
